response:
1. No hard interface-contract gaps were detected in the reported flow (`study.*`, `deckEditor.*`, `cardEditor.*`, `deckDetail.*`, `review.*`, `tabBar.*`, `csvExport.*`, `demoData.*` all appear), but there are integration risks.

2. High risk: CSV import still uses exact canonical-header detection (`front,back,note`) and will silently drop a valid first-card row that exactly matches those three fields; this is a functional ambiguity rather than a placeholder risk.

3. Medium risk: `csvExport.exportButton` is reused across two different UI states (pre-export `Button` and post-export `ShareLink`), so automation relying on “one stable control type per token” can misfire when asserting behavior across state transitions.

4. Medium risk: CSV export writes to `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory` with a name derived from deck title only, so repeated exports (same deck/title) can overwrite and potentially hand off stale/previous data if state isn’t fully cleared.

5. Medium risk: `CSVExportView` exports `fetchAllDecks(includeArchived: true)`, which may expose/archive export scope mismatch if contract/docs expect active decks only.

6. Medium risk: `DemoDataSeeder.removeAll()` depends on cascade delete behavior from `Deck` → `Card`/`ReviewLog`; if cascade config drifts, “remove demo data” may leave orphaned rows.

7. Low risk: demo-state is inferred via `Deck.isDemo`, so any pre-existing or externally inserted `isDemo == true` rows will make the toggle appear “enabled” and non-local to the seeder’s intended two-deck set.

8. No duplicated functional work conflicts observed between lanes A and B (A’s UI-flow wiring/comments and B’s settings/CSV/demo implementations are mostly disjoint).
